lead_headline: Dispatch extracted, auth simplified, and tests green — all before noon
lead_body: Dispatch left the marklab monorepo this morning as its own repository, with backend and frontend reorganized under apps/ and a Phase 1 foundation plan drafted, executed, and archived in seventeen commits. The auth layer shed its Cloudflare Access dependency in favor of trusting the deployment perimeter, and DISPATCH_MASTER_KEY is now a hard boot requirement.
lead_article:
The headline today is Dispatch itself: extracted from the marklab monorepo into its own repository, the backend and frontend reorganized under an apps/ folder, and a Phase 1 foundation plan drafted, implemented, and archived as complete — all before midday. The auth layer dropped its Cloudflare Access dependency in favor of trusting the deployment perimeter, DISPATCH_MASTER_KEY is now a hard boot requirement, and the test suite passed its first green run. Seventeen commits on a project restructure of this scope is a productive morning.

Workflow SDK had two merges worth noting: the getWritable() memoization fix closes a chunk-reordering bug that surfaces when the method is called repeatedly, and inline sourcemaps now propagate across all workspace packages via a backport of the build change. Claude Code shipped v2.1.150 overnight and then spent the rest of the day accumulating a dense backlog — thirty-six issues opened across billing false positives, context window silent downgrades after agents panel navigation, subprocess accumulation reaching 150 processes and 31 GB RAM, and a wave of troubleshooting PRs documenting the same. The MCP scheduled-routines approval bug and the AskUserQuestion empty-answer regression both closed. Astro resolved the domain-based i18n dynamic route 500 error and pushed a glob-loader negation fix, with two markdown abstraction PRs also queued. AI SDK moved quietly: a canary version bump and a broken-links docs fix.
